content.user_title: Generate OpenAPI Specs from Code and Contracts
content.value_statement: API teams need accurate OpenAPI contracts for docs, SDKs, and validation. This skill provides OpenAPI 3.1 templates, code-first examples, and linting workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides a complete OpenAPI 3.1 YAML template for a user management API.
Shows FastAPI patterns that expose OpenAPI schemas from Python models and routes.
Shows TypeScript tsoa decorators for generating OpenAPI from Express-style controllers.
Defines Spectral and Redocly validation examples for API linting and bundling.
Includes OpenAPI Generator commands for TypeScript, Python, and Go clients.
Summarizes practical OpenAPI design rules for schemas, examples, security, and operation IDs.
limitations: It provides documentation patterns, not a packaged generator or executable script.
Sample APIs use generic user-management models that require domain-specific changes.
Validation commands assume external tools are installed by the user.
It does not verify live API behavior against the generated contract.

use_cases.title: Draft a new REST contract
use_cases.description: Create a design-first OpenAPI 3.1 specification with paths, schemas, security, and examples before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Document an existing service
use_cases.description: Map FastAPI or TypeScript route code into structured OpenAPI operations, responses, request bodies, and generated schemas.

use_cases.title: Prepare SDK generation
use_cases.description: Lint, bundle, and refine an OpenAPI file so client libraries can be generated for multiple languages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an OpenAPI 3.1 starter spec for my REST API. Include info, servers, tags, security schemes, two resource paths, reusable schemas, and common error responses.

prompt_templates.title: Convert routes to OpenAPI
prompt_templates.scenario: Code-first documentation from an existing service
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these API routes and produce an OpenAPI 3.1 outline. Identify operation IDs, parameters, request bodies, responses, schemas, and missing examples.

prompt_templates.title: Improve contract quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this OpenAPI draft for completeness. Check security, reusable components, response coverage, schema constraints, examples, naming consistency, and linting issues.

prompt_templates.title: Plan SDK generation
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this OpenAPI spec for SDK generation. Recommend bundling steps, Spectral rules, Redocly checks, generator options, package naming, and breaking-change safeguards.

output_examples.input: A team needs documentation for users, profiles, authentication, and admin operations.
output_examples.output: A structured OpenAPI plan with server entries, grouped tags, reusable user schemas, security schemes, paginated list operations, and shared error responses.

output_examples.input: A FastAPI service has route handlers but incomplete public API documentation.
output_examples.output: A mapping from models and routes to OpenAPI operations, including parameter descriptions, response models, validation constraints, and example payload guidance.

output_examples.input: A release requires client SDKs for TypeScript, Python, and Go.
output_examples.output: A validation and generation checklist covering lint rules, bundled specs, generator targets, package names, output directories, and documentation preview steps.

best_practices: Define operation IDs, reusable schemas, shared responses, and security schemes before adding detailed examples.
Run linting and bundling checks before publishing documentation or generating SDKs.
Use realistic examples, explicit nullable fields, and consistent naming across paths, schemas, and parameters.
anti_patterns: Publishing generated specs without reviewing security requirements and error responses.
Duplicating schemas across endpoints instead of using shared components.
Hardcoding environment-specific server URLs without variables or clear descriptions.

faq.question: Does this skill generate an OpenAPI file automatically?
faq.answer: It provides templates, patterns, and prompts. The user or agent still applies them to the project.

faq.question: Which OpenAPI version does it target?
faq.answer: The examples target OpenAPI 3.1 and include modern schema, security, and validation patterns.

faq.question: Can it work with FastAPI?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes FastAPI examples that use Pydantic models, response models, route metadata, and generated OpenAPI output.

faq.question: Can it work with TypeScript services?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes tsoa-style TypeScript decorators for controllers, models, responses, and security metadata.

faq.question: Does it include validation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows Spectral and Redocly linting patterns for operation IDs, schemas, examples, media types, and responses.

faq.question: Does it create SDKs by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents OpenAPI Generator command patterns for TypeScript, Python, and Go clients.
